subject: science
topic: Modern agriculture has fundamentally altered human genetic expression
angle: While specific dietary components like polyphenols, fibers, and fats can modulate gut microbes and a ketogenic diet can rapidly reshape the human metabolome, the sources do not provide evidence that modern agriculture has fundamentally altered human genetic expression.
title: The Chemistry of Your Diet

hooks.text: Is your diet rewriting your DNA?
You assume agriculture changes your genes. The evidence does not support this.
You are choosing the microbes that live inside you.
A fork, a plate, and a shift in your internal chemistry.

reveal.headline: Dietary inputs influence your metabolome and gut microbes.
reveal.body: Specific fats and fibers modulate your gut bacteria and the chemicals derived from your food. There is no evidence that modern agriculture has altered your genetic expression.

explain.headline: Your food defines your internal chemistry.
explain.body: The food metabolome is the part of your chemistry derived from digestion. Dietary fibers and fat types change which bacteria live in your gut.

matters.headline: The source of your food matters.
matters.body: That may be why your internal environment shifts based on what you eat. Your body processes these specific inputs into a unique chemical profile.

example.headline: The contents of your bowl.
example.body: You sit at a table and eat a meal. Every fiber and fat source enters your system to be broken down by your microbes.

question.headline: What are you feeding your microbes today?

stat.label: the part of your metabolome derived from food digestion

claims.text: The quantity and type of fat modulate both beneficial and potentially detrimental microbes, as well as the Firmicutes/Bacteroides ratio in the gut.
claims.quote: The preclinical evidence suggests that both the quantity and type of fat modulate both beneficial and potentially detrimental microbes, as well as the Firmicutes/Bacteroides ratio in the gut.

claims.text: Dietary fibers like arabinoxylans, galacto-oligosaccharides, inulin, and oligofructose promote a range of beneficial bacteria and suppress potentially detrimental species.
claims.quote: Current research shows consistent clinical evidence that dietary fibers, including arabinoxylans, galacto-oligosaccharides, inulin, and oligofructose, promote a range of beneficial bacteria and suppress potentially detrimental species.

claims.text: The food metabolome is defined as the part of the human metabolome directly derived from the digestion and biotransformation of foods and their constituents.

verdict: The evidence shows that specific dietary inputs significantly influence the human metabolome and gut microbiota composition, but it does not establish a link to fundamental changes in human genetic expression.
caveat: The sources lack any data regarding long-term genetic expression or the specific impact of modern agricultural livestock production on human genetics.
caption:
Modern agriculture and its impact on human genetics is a frequent topic of discussion.

Research shows that specific dietary components like fats and fibers significantly influence the human metabolome and gut microbiota. However, the evidence does not establish a link to fundamental changes in human genetic expression, and data on long-term genetic impacts are missing.
